title: Decode HTTP content encoding in SDK downloads
body:
### Motivation and context

Closes #11482.

The SDK requests HTTP responses through urllib3 but writes downloads with `decode_content=False`. A proxy or server that applies gzip/deflate Content-Encoding therefore leaves the HTTP-compressed bytes in the requested dataset file instead of the archive content.

Decode HTTP Content-Encoding while reading the response. Treat progress totals as unknown for encoded responses, because their Content-Length describes compressed wire bytes rather than the decoded bytes written to disk.

### How has this been tested?

- Exact final commit: `45c2bb9855064975ebd31be8b005859c4231118c`.
- Native generated SDK and urllib3 HTTP transport against a local HTTP peer.
- Final validation: https://github.com/Afloat16/cvat/actions/runs/43398823652
- 20 new tests pass; original implementation: 11 failures and 9 passing controls.
- 48 existing mask/attribute SDK controls pass.
- Black and isort checks pass.

Cases cover gzip, deflate, identity, and absent Content-Encoding; Content-Length and chunked responses; explicit-file and directory targets; usable ZIP contents; decoded bodies exceeding the 10 MiB read size; progress counters; and atomic cleanup after malformed gzip. A native .gz file without HTTP Content-Encoding remains byte-for-byte compressed.

The original-source comparison now reports large payload mismatches through length/hash assertions to keep pytest's failure rendering bounded. The final exact-SHA run includes both implementations.

### Scope and risks

This concerns HTTP transfer encoding, not extraction of downloaded archives. The integration tests use a controlled local HTTP peer, not a deployed CVAT service. Encoded responses have indeterminate progress totals until their decoded length is known.
